items.name: agent-desktop
items.description: Operate desktop applications on macOS, Windows and Linux through native accessibility trees, using the agent-desktop CLI. Use when an AI agent must see or act on a desktop GUI: click buttons, fill forms, read UI state, navigate menus, toggle checkboxes, scroll, drag, type text, press shortcuts, take screenshots, manage windows, use the clipboard, launch or close apps, read notifications. Triggers on: "click button", "fill form", "open app", "read UI", "computer use", "operate desktop", "accessibility tree", "snapshot app", "type into field", "navigate menu", "toggle checkbox", "take screenshot", "desktop automation", "agent-desktop", or any desktop GUI task on macOS, Windows or Linux.

items.name: animate
items.description: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.

items.name: animate-expo
items.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo, making the decisions in the order that determines whether they feel right — should it animate, which thread it runs on, which properties, spring or timing, how the gesture hands off, how it degrades. Writes the implementation with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics. Use when animating anything in an Expo app, adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions, press feedback or haptics, or fixing motion that stutters on device. For web animation use `animate`.

items.name: animation-performance
items.description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — animate composite-only properties, keep motion off the main thread when the page is busy, and find the cause when an animation drops frames. Covers the layout/paint/composite pipeline, cheaper property swaps, CSS vs WAAPI vs requestAnimationFrame, Motion's hardware-accelerated path, React re-rendering per frame, inherited CSS variable recalculation, blur cost, and when `will-change` actually helps. Use when an animation is janky, choppy, stutters, or drops frames; when choosing which property to animate; when deciding between CSS and JS animation on performance grounds; or when reaching for `will-change` or GPU layers. For choosing easing, duration, or whether to animate at all use animate; for reviewing motion as a whole use review-animations.

items.name: animation-vocabulary
items.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

items.name: apple-design
items.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

items.name: ask-sonner
items.description: Guide to Sonner, the React toast library — install and wire up the Toaster, pick the right toast() call, promise and loading toasts, updating, dismissing and persisting toasts, styling, theming and icons, positioning and multiple toasters. Use when working with Sonner or troubleshooting it — toasts that don't appear, appear twice, lose their styles, ignore Tailwind classes, sit behind a modal, or don't follow dark mode.

items.name: book-to-skill
items.description: Converts books and documents (PDF, EPUB, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, plain text, RTF, MOBI/AZW with Calibre) into structured agent skills, extracting frameworks, mental models, principles, techniques, and anti-patterns. Use when the user wants to study a document through GitHub Copilot CLI, Amp, Claude Code, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, or OpenClaw, apply an author's frameworks while working, or build a reusable knowledge base from a file.

items.name: break-ui
items.description: Try to break a piece of UI by feeding it worst-case data — long names, unbreakable emails, one-letter names, missing fields, huge counts, zero items, long labels, non-Latin text, emoji, extreme numbers — then render it behind a "Demo data / Worst case" toggle and report everything that broke, with the fix for each. Use when the user asks to stress-test, break, or find edge cases in a component or screen, or to "try the worst case". For visual design critique use emil-design-eng; for motion use review-animations.

items.name: choreograph
items.description: Coordinate several elements that animate together — decide what moves, in what order, how much they overlap, and what stays still — so a group reads as one intentional motion instead of a pile of separate animations. Use when building or fixing a staggered list, a hero entrance, a view swap inside a container, a multi-step flow, an element leaving while its siblings close the gap, a morph between rich states, or any interaction with several moving parts (icon + background + lines, panel + content, items flying into a target). Triggers on — stagger, staggerChildren, delayChildren, animation-delay, sequence, sequencing, orchestration, choreography, cascade, wave, timeline, "one after another", "at the same time", crossfade, popLayout, mode="wait", AnimatePresence mode, hero entrance, list entrance, multi-step, step transition, morph, useAnimate, Promise.all animations, "feels mechanical", "feels robotic", "too much going on", "feels slow to open".

items.name: colab-operator
items.description: Operate Google Colab environments via the `colab` CLI. Use when asked to create or manage GPU/TPU sessions, run Python/shell on a remote Colab VM, sync files, automate environment setup (packages, auth, Drive), or export session history.

items.name: conventional-commit
items.description: Write a Conventional Commits message for the staged changes. Use when the user asks to commit, write a commit message, or summarize staged changes for git.

items.name: diagram-design
items.description: Create branded architecture, architecture delta, IT current-state, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER/data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar/spider, polar chart (polar/radial lollipop), loop/flywheel, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, exploded axonometric, axonometric plan, Venn, pyramid/funnel, treemap and marimekko, heatmap, bar and dumbbell, waterfall, line (slopegraph, ridgeline, streamgraph, bump), Gantt and scatter charts (bubble, beeswarm, box plot), high-level, process, medallion, data flow, DP integration, DP security matrix, Sankey, fishbone, Wardley map, kanban, user journey, service blueprint, deployment, dependency graph (arc diagram), UML class, story map, or database schema diagrams as HTML/SVG/PNG, with .drawio, Mermaid, and .excalidraw import, plus lifecycle phase maps, block decomposition trees, and onboarding guidance.

items.name: emil-design-eng
items.description: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.

items.name: find-animation-opportunities
items.description: Search a codebase or UI for places that don't animate but should, and reject everything that shouldn't. Read-only; it proposes motion with exact values, it does not implement it. Use when the user asks "what could be animated here?" or wants to "make this feel more alive". For fixing existing animations, use improve-animations or review-animations instead.

items.name: gestures
items.description: Build drag, swipe, and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1 and stay interruptible. Use when building or fixing anything the user drags, swipes, flings, holds, or dismisses with a gesture — drawers, sheets, swipe-to-dismiss toasts and cards, drag-to-reorder, pull-to-refresh, hold-to-confirm — or when a gesture feels laggy, disconnected from the finger, jumps on release, or can't be caught mid-animation. Triggers on — gesture, drag, draggable, swipe, swipe to dismiss, fling, momentum, velocity, drawer, sheet, bottom sheet, snap points, Vaul, dragConstraints, dragElastic, dragMomentum, onDragEnd, whileDrag, useMotionValue, rubber-band, overscroll, pull to refresh, hold to delete, press and hold, touch-action, dismiss threshold, "doesn't follow my finger", "jumps when I let go", "can't grab it mid-animation".

items.name: gpui-kit
items.description: How to build desktop applications with GPUI Kit, the Rust framework published as the gpui-kit crate (GPUI plus gpui_kit::component, gpui_kit::base, gpui_kit::assets). Use when setting up a gpui-kit app, choosing or using a component (Button, Input, Select, Dialog, Sheet, Tabs, Sidebar, List, DataTable, Tree, Chart, etc.), handling component state, theming, or window overlays, and for GPUI mechanics: actions and keybindings, async tasks, contexts, custom elements, entities, events, focus, global state, layout and styling, ElementId, and tests including UI integration testing. Holds the normative Coding Guides: read them before any architecture, state-ownership, public API, naming, or testing decision. Pairs with the gpui-kit-design-guides skill for the Design Guides.

items.name: gpui-kit-design-guides
items.description: The normative Design Guides for GPUI Kit desktop applications. Read in full before designing or changing any screen, layout, spacing, visual hierarchy, color, density, component choice, interaction state, overlay, motion, data-heavy view, or interface copy in a GPUI Kit (gpui-kit / gpui-component) application, and before reviewing UI work for design quality. Also use when asked what the design rules are, or whether a UI decision follows them.

items.name: humanizer
items.description:
Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads like the writer without changing what it says.
Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells: not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line
closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes everywhere, inflated claims, sales
language, stock AI words, bold labels, or filler. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing."

items.name: improve-animations
items.description: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents (or cheaper models) to execute. Read-only on source code — it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to "improve the animations", "audit the motion", "make this app feel better", or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.

items.name: mcp-builder
items.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).

items.name: migrate-to-rust
items.description: Clones, analyzes, plans, and migrates legacy codebases (C++, Fortran, Java, Python, C, Shell) from a GitHub URL or local directory to a modern, high-performance, deterministic, 100% Safe Rust architecture, tracking live telemetry across every task bucket, test failure/fix cycle, and Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) stage, and producing a first-person AI storytelling report and interactive HTML infographic. Use when migrating a GitHub repository or local codebase to Rust, porting legacy C++, Fortran, Python, or Java workloads to memory-safe Rust, designing Struct-of-Arrays (SoA) or SIMD Rust architectures, or optimizing Rust ports with LLVM PGO. Don't use for unrelated non-Rust refactoring or single-line syntax questions.

items.name: mobile-native
items.description: Make a web app feel native on a phone — the small CSS and meta-tag fixes that separate "a website in a browser" from something that feels installed. Covers sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, pull-to-refresh hijacking scroll, content under the notch, long-press selecting button text, carousels that scroll the wrong way, mismatched status bars, and the rule that you test on real hardware. Use when a web app is being built for or reviewed on mobile, when something "works in Chrome but feels wrong on my phone", when building a PWA, a bottom sheet, a carousel, a full-screen layout, or any touch interaction. For motion itself use animate; for React Native use animate-expo.

items.name: nsh
items.description: Build, run, test and package Native Shell (NSH) apps in Rust, TSX or both. Use for NSH development requests and projects with nsh.json, nsh-* crate dependencies or imports from nsh modules. Covers NSH reactivity, components, styling and tooling, with Coding Guides and working app recipes.

items.name: nsh-design-guides
items.description: The normative Design Guides for Native Shell (NSH) apps. Read before designing or changing any screen, layout, spacing, visual hierarchy, color, density, component choice, interaction state, overlay, motion, data-heavy view or interface copy in an NSH app, in TSX or Rust, and before reviewing UI work for design quality. Also use when asked what the design rules are, or whether a UI decision follows them.

items.name: pick-ui-library
items.description: Pick the right library for a given frontend task from a curated, opinionated list — numbers, OTP inputs, charts, command menus, virtualization, drag and drop, toasts, state, styling, and more. Only runs when explicitly invoked; it does not trigger on its own.

items.name: prototype
items.description: Build multiple genuinely different versions of a UI piece you describe, rendered behind a visual picker so you can flip through them live and promote the one that feels right. Only runs when explicitly invoked; it does not trigger on its own.

items.name: readme-writer
items.description: Draft or improve a project README by inspecting the repository. Use when the user asks to write, rewrite, or improve a README or project documentation landing page.

items.name: remove-animations
items.description: Find the animations an interface doesn't need and remove them — motion on keyboard actions, high-frequency surfaces, functional data, and decoration with no purpose — then clean up what they leave behind. Edits code, but only to subtract; it never adds or retunes motion. Use when the user says the app "feels slow", "has too much animation", "feels over-animated", wants to "tone down the motion", or asks what animations to remove. For finding places that should animate, use find-animation-opportunities; for fixing animations that should stay, use improve-animations or review-animations.

items.name: review-animations
items.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

items.name: sag
items.description: Set up the standalone SAG CLI and search local project files by meaning. Use for SAG installation, project search setup, understanding unfamiliar implementations, or managing indexed folders and ignore rules.

items.name: security-audit
items.description: Security guidance and vulnerability review for codebases, APIs, services, CLI tools, libraries, and daemons. Use for security questions, focused reviews, vulnerability research, security audits, or pen tests. Run the complete workflow only for explicit codebase audit or pen-test requests, full/comprehensive/end-to-end reviews, or requested report artifacts.

items.name: solidcraft-checking
items.description: Use alongside solidcraft-modeling and solidcraft-editing whenever you build, change or port a SolidCraft design. Checks for errors SolidCraft does not report (parameter ranges, every allowed value, exact STEP comparison), regression tests, designs kept in git, porting from build123d, CadQuery, OpenSCAD or STEP.

items.name: solidcraft-editing
items.description: Use when changing, fixing or extending an existing SolidCraft design through its MCP server - a .sc file (or an older .solidcraft one) or the design open in the app. Typical requests: resize it, move a cut, change a hole or standoff, add a fillet or chamfer, make a fixed value parametric, or a feature shows an error after a change or after the app crashed.

items.name: solidcraft-mechanisms
items.description: Use when building, driving or animating an assembly or mechanism in SolidCraft through its MCP server - components, grounding, joints and joint origins, rigid groups, motion links, closed loops such as an actuator on a hinged panel or a linkage, contact sets, motion studies, degrees of freedom - or when a drive moves nothing, stops early or a part jumps when it is joined. To model the parts themselves, use solidcraft-modeling.

items.name: solidcraft-modeling
items.description: Use when building a new part, enclosure, bracket, plate, flange or any other 3D solid in SolidCraft through its MCP server (tools such as batch, execute, measure, screenshot), or when a SolidCraft session is using many tool calls or tokens.

items.name: untangle-codebase
items.description: Untangle a whole codebase in one pass, so agents working in it read less per change, break less without noticing, and debug faster.

items.name: utools-plugin-dev
items.description: 开发和维护 uTools 插件应用时使用。适用于已有插件项目的功能实现、代码修改、uTools API 集成、问题排查与开发规范查询。

items.name: write-swift
items.description: How to write modern Swift well — modeling with value types, Swift 6 data-race safety and approachable concurrency (@concurrent, main-actor-by-default, actors, task groups), protocols and generics (some vs any), API design, performance and ARC, Swift Testing, macros, and the modern language features agents don't know about yet. Use when writing, reviewing, or migrating Swift, or when a concurrency error, a hang, a data race, a retain cycle, or a performance problem needs fixing.

items.name: wxjava-integration-guide
items.description: 为 Java、Spring Boot 或 Solon 项目生成可验证的 WxJava 接入方案，包括模块选择、BOM、配置、最小调用代码以及单/多账号集成。适用于用户要求接入公众号、小程序、支付、企业微信、开放平台、视频号或微信小店时。

items.name: code-reviewer
items.description: Reviews code changes for bugs, security issues and maintainability. Use proactively after writing or modifying code, or when the user asks for a review.

items.name: debugger
items.description: Root-cause analysis for errors, failing tests and unexpected behavior. Use when something is broken and the cause is not obvious.

items.name: explain
items.description: Explain how a file, function or feature works, with a short walkthrough.

items.name: fix-issue
items.description: Investigate and fix a GitHub issue end to end — reproduce, fix, test.

items.name: agent-desktop
items.description: agent-desktop 的 MCP server（stdio）：每个命令都是一个工具（desktop_snapshot、desktop_click、desktop_session_start…），通过无障碍树查看和操作 macOS / Windows / Linux 桌面应用。

items.name: browser-harness
items.description: browser-harness 的 MCP server（stdio）：让 Cursor 等 MCP 客户端通过 CDP 控制你的 Chrome 或 Browser Use 云浏览器。

items.name: context7
items.description: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples pulled into the prompt.

items.name: craft-anything
items.description: Craft Anything 的 MCP server：320 个工具，用于研究网站/应用/游戏的实现（页面、代码、文件、运行行为），并驱动编码 Agent 重建（rebuild）。需要先安装 tool/craft-anything。

items.name: fetch
items.description: Fetch web pages and convert them to markdown for the model (official reference server, needs uv).

items.name: filesystem
items.description: Read, write and search files inside allowed directories (official reference server).

items.name: github
items.description: GitHub's official remote MCP server: repos, issues, pull requests, actions, code search.

items.name: goofish-sandbox
items.description: 闲鱼 MCP server（Docker 沙箱模式）：浏览器自动化在容器虚拟桌面中运行，不占用本机浏览器。与 mcp/goofish 使用同一个 server 名，二者互相替换。

items.name: goofish
items.description: 闲鱼（Goofish/Xianyu）MCP server（本机模式）：商品查询/发布/下架、搜索、图片上传、AI 类目识别、IM 消息收发等 17 个工具，由 goofish-cli 提供。

items.name: graphify
items.description: Graphify 的 MCP server（stdio）：把当前项目的知识图谱 graphify-out/graph.json 提供给 Agent，支持 query_graph 等图查询工具。

items.name: iconmcp
items.description: IconMCP 的远程 MCP server（无需登录）：按含义搜索约 6,800 个原创图标（search_icons），取 SVG 或 React 组件（get_icon），浏览主题图标集（list_sets / get_set）；找不到时可以请求新图标（request_icon），也能反馈或修正图标。

items.name: kit-tools
items.description: Example self-hosted MCP server shipped in this repo (zero dependencies): current time, UUIDs, text hashing.

items.name: playwright
items.description: Browser automation via Playwright accessibility snapshots (Microsoft).

items.name: prompts-chat
items.description: prompts.chat 的远程 MCP server：搜索和获取提示词、Agent skill 和 Bot，改进提示词；登录后还能保存自己的提示词和 skill。

items.name: rea
items.description: REA 的 MCP server（stdio）：逆向分析原生二进制、JavaScript / Electron 应用、.NET 程序集和网站，结果附带证据与局限。

items.name: scenario
items.description: Scenario（scenario.com）的远程 MCP server：生成和编辑图片、视频、音频、贴图、天空盒、3D 模型、精灵图等游戏素材，选模型、跑 LoRA、训练自定义模型、管理团队用量。需要 Scenario 账号（OAuth 登录）。

items.name: solidcraft
items.description: SolidCraft 的 MCP server（stdio）：Agent 用和界面相同的命令建模（batch、execute、measure、screenshot…）；无界面时自带设计会话，桌面应用运行时自动连接，可以看着 Agent 建模。

items.name: treg
items.description: treg（"工具界的 OpenRouter"）的远程 MCP server：用一个账号按次付费调用数千个第三方 API（SEO 与外链、社媒与趋势、人员与公司信息补全、广告库、网页抓取、图片视频生成），以及团队自己登记的密钥、CLI 和 skill。

items.name: block-dangerous-commands
items.description: Blocks destructive shell commands (rm -rf /, force-push to main, mkfs, dd to disks, curl | sh …) before the agent runs them.

items.name: notify-on-stop
items.description: Desktop notification when the agent finishes a turn or needs your input (macOS, Linux, Windows).

items.name: cad-modeling
items.description: 用 SolidCraft 做参数化 3D CAD 建模：MCP server，加上官方推荐的 4 个建模 skill（新建零件、修改设计、参数与 STEP 校验、装配与机构）。需要先安装 SolidCraft。

items.name: design-engineering
items.description: Emil Kowalski 的设计工程 skill（18 个）：动画从零构建、手势交互、编排、性能、审查与精简，Apple 设计原则，移动端原生体验，破坏性测试 UI，多版本原型，UI 库选择，Sonner，现代 Swift。

items.name: desktop-automation
items.description: 桌面 computer use：用 Vercel Labs 的 agent-desktop 通过无障碍树查看和操作 macOS / Windows / Linux 桌面应用（skill + MCP server）。插件自带 agent-desktop 1.2.0，安装时由 Claude Code 自动下载，不需要另外安装 CLI（需要 Node.js）。

items.name: dev-essentials
items.description: Everyday development bundle: /review and /test commands, a test-writer sub-agent and a changelog skill.

items.name: rust-migration
items.description: 把 C/C++、Fortran、Java、Python、Shell 等遗留代码迁移到 Safe Rust：分析、规划、迁移、PGO 与遥测报告。

items.name: rust-native-ui
items.description: 长桥 Longbridge 的 Rust 原生 UI 开发：Native Shell（NSH，iOS / Android / 桌面 / Web / 终端跨平台）和 GPUI Kit（GPUI 桌面应用框架）各自的编码 skill 与设计规范 skill。

items.name: security
items.description: 安全审计：对代码库、API、服务、CLI、库和守护进程做漏洞审查与安全评估，按信任边界给出证据、复现方式、优先级和最小修复（Cloudflare security-audit skill）。

items.name: utools
items.description: uTools 插件应用开发：uTools 官方的 utools-plugin-dev skill，内置 uTools 8.0+ 的 API 参考和开发规范，辅助编写、修改和排查 uTools 插件。

items.name: wxjava
items.description: WxJava 微信开发：为 Java / Spring Boot / Solon 项目生成公众号、小程序、支付、企业微信、开放平台等的最小接入方案。

items.name: agent-context
items.description: Print a compact project snapshot (tree, manifests, recent commits) to paste into any AI chat.

items.name: git-prune-branches
items.description: Delete local git branches whose upstream is gone or that are merged into the default branch.

items.name: agent-desktop
items.description: Vercel Labs 的桌面 computer use 工具：通过操作系统无障碍树（macOS AX / Windows UI Automation / Linux AT-SPI）读取并操作桌面应用，输出带 ref 的 JSON，不依赖截图或像素匹配；提供 CLI、C 库和 MCP server。

items.name: browser-harness
items.description: Browser Use 出的浏览器控制工具：通过 Chrome DevTools Protocol 直接驱动你正在用的 Chrome（带登录态），也能连 Browser Use 云浏览器。截图 + 坐标点击、持久化 Python 会话，Agent 缺什么 helper 就自己写进工作区，越用越顺手。附带 skill 和 MCP server。

items.name: caveman
items.description: Caveman：让 AI 编码 Agent 少说、少读、少花钱。回答压缩成「原始人」短句（代码、命令、报错原样保留）；日志、JSON、CSV、测试输出在模型读到前先压缩；Auto 按问题难度选模型和推理强度；Blocks 复用 Agent 写过的脚本；另有网页压缩、记忆文件压缩、token 用量分析。一条命令接入 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 等 30 多个 Agent。

items.name: colab-cli
items.description: Google Colab 官方 CLI：在终端里开 Colab 的 CPU / GPU（T4、L4、G4、A100、H100）/ TPU（v5e1、v6e1）运行时，执行本地 Python 脚本、Jupyter 笔记本或管道输入的代码，开 REPL 或 SSH，上传下载远程文件，挂载 Google Drive、授权 GCP；colab run 一条命令完成开机 → 跑脚本 → 取回输出 → 关机。适合把训练、数据处理交给 AI Agent 在云端 GPU 上跑。

items.name: goofish-cli
items.description: 闲鱼（Goofish/Xianyu）自动化 CLI，原生支持 MCP：商品发布/下架/查询、图片上传、AI 类目识别、IM 实时收发、风控限流，内置 5 个 Claude Skills。

items.name: graphify
items.description: Graphify：把整个项目（代码、文档、PDF、图片、视频）转成可查询的知识图谱，让 Agent 查图而不是逐个 grep / 读文件。代码用 tree-sitter 在本地解析（约 40 种语言，不调用 LLM），每条边标明是源码里明写的（EXTRACTED）还是推断的（INFERRED）；输出可交互的 graph.html、要点报告 GRAPH_REPORT.md 和 graph.json，支持 query / path / explain 查询。

items.name: impeccable
items.description: Impeccable：给编码 Agent 的前端设计词汇和审查工具。一个 skill 带 24 个命令：bolder / quieter / distill / colorize / typeset / layout 调整风格，critique 打分式 UX 评审，audit 检查无障碍、性能、主题和响应式（P0–P3 分级），polish / harden / clarify / adapt / optimize 收尾，live 在浏览器里选中元素实时切换变体；另有 62 条确定性规则的「AI 味」检测器（Inter 字体、紫蓝渐变、卡片套卡片等），可在 Agent hook、命令行 / CI 和 Chrome 扩展里运行。

items.description: REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）：给 Agent 用的逆向工程工具，一个 MCP 覆盖原生二进制、JavaScript / Electron 应用、.NET 程序集和网站，本地分析并给出每个结论的证据和局限；也可以在终端直接用。看到别的应用里喜欢的功能，可以让 Agent 搞清它怎么实现并在自己的项目里做一个。

items.name: sag-wiki
items.description: SAG-Wiki：给人和 Agent 用的轻量本地知识库。添加一个文件夹就能检索里面的文档、笔记和代码，建索引和检索都不调用 LLM、不需要向量库（约 200 ms 索引一百万字），用自研的 SAG2 证据检索跨文件找出处；问答答案可追溯到原文段落。桌面版（macOS / Windows，约 14 MB）支持快速搜索、带引用的问答、Markdown 编辑和文档关系浏览；PDF、Office、EPUB 开箱转换。CLI sag 可单独使用，让 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 检索同一个知识库。
